title: Mapping the Information Geometry of an Unresolved Dark Matter Population using a Differentiable Strong Lensing Simulator
comment: 21 pages, 11 figures. Submitted to ApJ
summary: Strong gravitational lensing is a unique probe of the matter power spectrum on small scales, where the abundance of dark matter subhalos in galaxies could be used to distinguish the predictions of the concordance cold dark matter model from alternatives such as warm dark matter. Extracting this signal poses major computational challenges, since perturbations of the lensing potential induced by substructure can be degenerate with both the macro-model of the lens and highly flexible models of the background source. Here, we introduce a framework to quantify these degeneracies using a differentiable strong-lensing simulator. Substructure is represented in a spectral basis confined to an annular domain surrounding the lensed image, allowing signals from a population of NFW subhalos to be encoded in a finite vector space. We then use the Fisher matrix to determine how much information about substructure is absorbed by nuisance components of the model. We find that macro-model degeneracies are largely confined to low-order perturbations of the lensing potential, while degeneracies with the source model can strongly suppress sensitivity across a broad range of scales as the expressivity of the source model is increased. Finally, we introduce the Fisher Graph Laplacian prior as a diagnostic tool to study how the internal degeneracies of the source model can be used to regulate the sensitivity of the data to an unresolved population of dark matter subhalos.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a differentiable strong-lensing simulator to quantify degeneracies between dark matter substructure signals and nuisance components (macro-model and background source model) in strong gravitational lensing analyses. Using a spectral basis for substructure representation and the Fisher matrix, the authors show that macro-model degeneracies are confined to low-order perturbations, while source-model degeneracies can strongly suppress sensitivity across broad scales. They also introduce the Fisher Graph Laplacian prior as a diagnostic tool to regulate sensitivity to unresolved dark matter subhalo populations.
AI.motivation: Strong gravitational lensing can probe the small-scale matter power spectrum and distinguish cold dark matter from warm dark matter via subhalo abundances, but extracting this signal faces major computational challenges because substructure-induced perturbations of the lensing potential can be degenerate with the macro-model of the lens and flexible background source models.
AI.method: The framework uses a differentiable strong-lensing simulator where substructure is represented in a spectral basis confined to an annular domain around the lensed image, encoding NFW subhalo populations in a finite vector space. The Fisher matrix is then used to quantify how much substructure information is absorbed by nuisance model components, and the Fisher Graph Laplacian prior is introduced as a diagnostic tool for regulating sensitivity to unresolved subhalo populations.
AI.result: Macro-model degeneracies are largely confined to low-order perturbations of the lensing potential, whereas degeneracies with the source model can strongly suppress sensitivity across a broad range of scales as source-model expressivity increases.
AI.conclusion: The Fisher Graph Laplacian prior provides a principled way to regulate data sensitivity to unresolved dark matter subhalo populations, accounting for internal degeneracies of the source model.

title: Testing MOND-like modifications to gravity using growth-rate measurements and one-loop corrections to the matter power spectrum
comment: 22 pages, 7 figures and 2 table. Comments are welcome!
summary: We develop a perturbative framework for structure formation in a broad class of MOND-like theories characterized by a generalized nonlinear Poisson equation. We derive the modified evolution equations governing matter perturbations and obtain the corresponding linear growth equation, extending the analysis into the mildly nonlinear regime through one-loop corrections to the matter power spectrum. Beyond the theoretical framework, we perform a cosmological analysis based on two phenomenological scenarios: one parametrized by a quantity controlling the degree of nonlinearity in the generalized Poisson equation, and another describing the interplay between the MOND acceleration scale and the cosmological acceleration associated with the background expansion. We constrain these scenarios using recent measurements of the growth rate of structure, $fσ_8$, DESI-DR2 baryon acoustic oscillation data, and Type Ia supernova compilations. We find no statistically significant evidence for departures from the standard $Λ$CDM cosmology. The inferred constraints are fully consistent with the GR + $Λ$CDM scenario within the current observational uncertainties. At nonlinear scales, we note that MOND-like modifications can alter $P_{\rm NL}(k)$ and leave signatures that current and future high-precision large-scale-structure observations may probe. Our results establish a systematic connection between MOND-like gravitational dynamics and large-scale structure observations, providing a consistent framework to assess the phenomenological viability of MOND-inspired modifications of gravity in a cosmological context.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a perturbative framework for structure formation in MOND-like theories with a generalized nonlinear Poisson equation, derives modified perturbation evolution and one-loop corrections to the matter power spectrum, and constrains two phenomenological scenarios using fσ8 growth data, DESI-DR2 BAO, and SNe Ia observations. No statistically significant deviation from ΛCDM is found, though MOND-like effects may leave signatures at nonlinear scales.
AI.motivation: To establish a systematic and consistent framework connecting MOND-like modified gravity dynamics to large-scale structure observations, enabling a rigorous assessment of whether such theories are phenomenologically viable in a cosmological context.
AI.method: A generalized nonlinear Poisson equation is used to derive modified evolution equations for matter perturbations and a linear growth equation. The analysis is extended into the mildly nonlinear regime via one-loop corrections to the matter power spectrum. Two phenomenological scenarios are defined (one parametrized by the degree of nonlinearity in the Poisson equation, another by the interplay between the MOND acceleration scale and cosmological acceleration), and constrained with fσ8 growth data, DESI-DR2 BAO, and Type Ia supernova compilations.
AI.result: No statistically significant evidence for departure from standard ΛCDM is found; constraints are fully consistent with GR+ΛCDM within current observational uncertainties. At nonlinear scales, MOND-like modifications can alter P_NL(k), leaving potential signatures detectable by current and future high-precision large-scale-structure surveys.
AI.conclusion: The framework establishes a systematic connection between MOND-like gravitational dynamics and large-scale structure observations, providing a consistent basis for assessing the phenomenological viability of MOND-inspired modified gravity in cosmology.

title: CosmoPyro: Gradients for Gravitational-Wave Cosmology
comment: 18 + 23 pages, 7 + 7 figures
summary: Gravitational-wave (GW) observations of stellar-mass compact binary coalescences directly measure the source luminosity distance. Combined with the source redshift, these measurements constrain the current expansion rate of the Universe, the Hubble constant, $H_0$, or $h=H_0 / [100 \,{\rm km \,s^{-1} \, Mpc^{-1}}]$. For most GW signals no electromagnetic redshift measurement is expected, but the GW signal itself depends on the redshifted (detector-frame) masses. Assuming a source-frame mass distribution therefore enables a redshift estimate for each source. Combining the redshift estimates with the distance measurements provides a weak constraint on $H_0$ for each individual source that tightens with the number of sources in the catalog. However, the shape of the source-frame mass distribution is not known a priori, and previous work has relied on parametric models (piecewise power-laws with Gaussian components), and one-dimensional Gaussian processes. Here, we introduce CosmoPyro, a fully differentiable hierarchical Bayesian inference code that models the mass distribution using either one- or two-dimensional Gaussian processes. With the latest GW transient catalog (GWTC-5) we find $h = 0.66^{+0.17}_{-0.20}$ and $h = 0.57^{+0.20}_{-0.15}$ (median with $1σ$ uncertainty), for the one- and two-dimensional case, respectively. Despite the noticeably different inferred mass distributions, both models yield $H_0$ values consistent with the latest LVK measurements within $1 σ$. While our main results marginalize over the Gaussian-process power-spectrum hyperparameters, the measurement is also robust against fixing these hyperparameters over a range comparable to their measured uncertainty.

AI.tldr: CosmoPyro is a fully differentiable hierarchical Bayesian inference code that models the source-frame mass distribution of gravitational-wave sources using 1D or 2D Gaussian processes, enabling redshift estimates and Hubble constant constraints from GW catalogs without assuming parametric mass distribution models.
AI.motivation: Gravitational-wave observations can constrain the Hubble constant by combining luminosity distance with redshift estimates. However, estimating redshift from GW signals relies on knowing the source-frame mass distribution, which is not known a priori. Previous approaches used parametric models or 1D Gaussian processes, limiting flexibility in modeling the mass distribution.
AI.method: The paper introduces CosmoPyro, a fully differentiable hierarchical Bayesian inference code that models the mass distribution using either one- or two-dimensional Gaussian processes. The code combines redshift estimates from the mass distribution with distance measurements to constrain H0, and marginalizes over Gaussian-process power-spectrum hyperparameters.
AI.result: Using GWTC-5, the code finds h = 0.66^{+0.17}_{-0.20} (1D case) and h = 0.57^{+0.20}_{-0.15} (2D case). Both models yield H0 values consistent with the latest LVK measurements within 1σ, despite noticeably different inferred mass distributions. The measurement remains robust against fixing the GP power-spectrum hyperparameters over a range comparable to their uncertainty.
AI.conclusion: The flexible Gaussian process-based approach provides a robust alternative to parametric mass distribution modeling for estimating H0 from GW catalogs, yielding results consistent with LVK measurements while accommodating uncertainty in the mass distribution shape.

title: PowerFull: fast and accurate computation of the relativistic angular galaxy power spectrum including local primordial non-Gaussianity
comment: 77 pages, 20 figures, 4 tables
summary: Current and forthcoming wide-field galaxy surveys, such as SPHEREx and Euclid, provide a unique opportunity to probe the ultra-large scales of structure formation, where primordial non-Gaussianity, often parameterized by $f_\text{NL}$, is expected to leave its most detectable imprint. At the same time, these surveys inevitably enter regimes where relativistic and wide-angle effects become significant, requiring careful modeling to extract unbiased cosmological information. We address these challenges by applying the total-angular-momentum (TAM) formalism to describe redshift-space clustering beyond the flat-sky approximation. The standard Fourier-mode description, which characterizes distortions by the angle between a mode and a line of sight, becomes ill-defined over wide fields, whereas the TAM basis naturally separates radial and angular contributions and incorporates the relevant relativistic effects. Within this framework, we provide a new parameterization of wide-angle predictions that can be compared directly with survey data. We then introduce PowerFull, a modification of the Julia-based 2-FAST package, which enables efficient computation of the full relativistic angular power spectrum. Finally, using Fisher information matrix-based analyses, we show that a survey like SPHEREx reaches $σ(f_\text{NL}) \sim 1$, but that neglecting the relativistic and wide-angle contributions shifts the recovered $f_\text{NL}$ by an amount of order its own uncertainty: at this precision the inferred value is biased unless the clustering is modeled consistently.

AI.tldr: This paper applies the total-angular-momentum (TAM) formalism to model redshift-space clustering beyond the flat-sky approximation for wide-field galaxy surveys like SPHEREx and Euclid. The authors provide a new parameterization of wide-angle predictions, introduce PowerFull (a modification of the Julia-based 2-FAST package) for efficient computation of the full relativistic angular power spectrum, and show via Fisher analysis that while SPHEREx can reach σ(f_NL) ~ 1, neglecting relativistic and wide-angle effects biases the recovered f_NL by an amount comparable to its own uncertainty.
AI.motivation: Wide-field galaxy surveys probe ultra-large scales where primordial non-Gaussianity (f_NL) leaves its most detectable imprint, but these regimes also exhibit significant relativistic and wide-angle effects. The standard Fourier-mode description becomes ill-defined over wide fields, motivating the need for a framework (TAM formalism) that naturally handles these effects to extract unbiased cosmological information.
AI.method: The authors use the total-angular-momentum (TAM) formalism to describe redshift-space clustering beyond the flat-sky approximation, separating radial and angular contributions and incorporating relativistic effects. They introduce a new parameterization of wide-angle predictions adaptable to survey data, and develop PowerFull, a modification of the Julia-based 2-FAST package, for efficient computation of the full relativistic angular power spectrum. Fisher information matrix analyses are employed to assess parameter constraints and biases.
AI.result: Fisher information matrix analyses show that a survey like SPHEREx can reach σ(f_NL) ~ 1, but neglecting relativistic and wide-angle contributions shifts the recovered f_NL by an amount of order its own uncertainty, meaning the inferred value is biased at this precision unless clustering is modeled consistently.
AI.conclusion: Consistent modeling of relativistic and wide-angle effects is essential for unbiased f_NL constraints from next-generation wide-field surveys. The TAM-based framework and PowerFull provide the necessary tools for this task.

title: Recurrent Multi-year Mg II BAL Variability in SDSS J1333+0012
comment: 5 Figures, 1 Table, Accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: We present a long-term spectroscopic study of Broad Absorption Line (BAL) variability in the quasar J1333+0012 (\zem = 0.9197) using an extensive multi-epoch dataset spanning nearly two decades. The dataset comprises multi-epoch observations from multiple observatories, delivering nearly uniform temporal coverage of the Mg II BAL profile, with close to one spectroscopic observation per year spanning the period from 2008 to 2025. We identify recurrent multi-year variability in the BAL absorption strength, characterized by a rest-frame timescale of $\sim$4 yr. Because the well-sampled baseline covers only a small number of candidate cycles, we present J1333+0012 as a candidate quasi-periodic BAL system. In contrast, contemporaneous optical photometric light curves from CRTS, Pan-STARRS, ZTF, and PTF show no statistically significant correlated variability on comparable timescales. However, ionization-driven variability cannot be ruled out, as the observed optical continuum does not directly trace the unobserved extreme-UV ionizing continuum. The coherence of the variability across distinct velocity components, coupled with the absence of large-scale profile reshaping, is consistent with a geometric origin. We interpret the observed behavior as modulation of the line-of-sight absorption by the rotation of an inhomogeneous shielding-gas structure.

AI.tldr: A nearly two-decade spectroscopic study of the quasar J1333+0012 reveals recurrent multi-year (~4 yr rest-frame) variability in its Mg II BAL profile, presented as a candidate quasi-periodic BAL system, with a geometric interpretation involving rotation of an inhomogeneous shielding-gas structure.
AI.motivation: To characterize long-term BAL variability in quasars, identify candidate quasi-periodic systems, and distinguish between ionization-driven and geometric origins of absorption variability.
AI.method: Multi-epoch spectroscopic monitoring (2008-2025) from multiple observatories providing near-uniform yearly coverage of the Mg II BAL profile, combined with contemporaneous optical photometric light curves from CRTS, Pan-STARRS, ZTF, and PTF for cross-correlation analysis.
AI.result: Identified recurrent ~4 yr (rest-frame) variability in BAL absorption strength; no statistically significant correlated optical continuum variability on comparable timescales; coherence of variability across velocity components with no large-scale profile reshaping.
AI.conclusion: The variability is consistent with a geometric origin, interpreted as modulation of line-of-sight absorption by rotation of an inhomogeneous shielding-gas structure, though ionization-driven variability cannot be definitively ruled out.

title: Broadband Chiral Primordial Gravitational Waves from Constant-roll Inflation in Parity-violating Symmetric Teleparallel Gravity
comment: 8 pages, 4 figures
summary: We investigate primordial gravitational waves (GWs) generated during constant-roll inflation in a parity-violating extension of symmetric teleparallel gravity. The parity-violating interactions leave the background evolution and linear scalar perturbations unchanged, while inducing velocity birefringence in the tensor sector. Consequently, one of the two circular polarization states undergoes tachyonic amplification, producing a strongly blue and nearly fully chiral tensor spectrum from the cosmic microwave background (CMB) to interferometer scales. We identify viable constant-roll parameter regions consistent with current CMB constraints and determine the largest coupling strength compatible with both CMB B-mode measurements and the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) O1--O4a bound on the stochastic GW background. The predicted CMB B-mode spectra may be detectable by LiteBIRD, while the enhanced high-frequency signal could be accessible to the LISA--Taiji network and LVK O5 run. The model also predicts nonvanishing TB and EB correlations. These results highlight the potential of combining CMB and multi-band GW observations to test parity-violating gravity during inflation.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates primordial gravitational waves generated during constant-roll inflation in a parity-violating extension of symmetric teleparallel gravity. Parity-violating interactions cause velocity birefringence in the tensor sector, leading to tachyonic amplification of one circular polarization state and producing a strongly blue, nearly fully chiral GW spectrum. The authors identify viable parameter regions consistent with CMB constraints and LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA bounds, showing the model may be detectable by LiteBIRD, LISA-Taiji, and LVK O5, with predicted TB and EB correlations.
AI.motivation: To test parity-violating gravity during inflation by combining CMB and multi-band gravitational wave observations, since such parity violation could be a signature of fundamental physics beyond general relativity.
AI.method: The study considers constant-roll inflation in a parity-violating extension of symmetric teleparallel gravity, where parity-violating interactions induce velocity birefringence in tensor perturbations while leaving the background and scalar sector unchanged. It identifies viable constant-roll parameter regions consistent with CMB measurements and determines coupling strength limits from CMB B-mode data and LVK O1-O4a stochastic background bounds.
AI.result: The model produces a strongly blue and nearly fully chiral tensor spectrum spanning CMB to interferometer scales. The predicted CMB B-mode spectra may be detectable by LiteBIRD, while the high-frequency signal could be accessible to LISA-Taiji and LVK O5. The model also predicts nonvanishing TB and EB correlations.
AI.conclusion: Combining CMB and multi-band GW observations offers a promising avenue to test parity-violating gravity during inflation, with the model providing distinct observational signatures across multiple future experiments.

title: Quasar Impostors: Two Extremely UV-Bright ($M_{\rm UV}\approx-23.5$) Reionisation-Epoch Galaxies Powered by Very Massive Stars
comment: 18 figures, 4 tables. Submitted
summary: The extreme bright end of the galaxy UV luminosity function during reionisation remains poorly constrained, particularly where the galaxy and quasar luminosity functions overlap and source classification becomes ambiguous. We present JWST/NIRSpec and ALMA Band-6 observations of J1450-0144 ($z=6.627$) and J1429-0104 ($z=6.796$), two $M_{\rm UV}\simeq-23.5$ sources originally classified as faint quasars by SHELLQs. NIRSpec reveals blue UV continua, strong P Cygni profiles in N V, Si IV, and C IV, broad He II $\lambda1640$ emission with rest-frame equivalent widths of $8.8\pm1.2$ and $3.7\pm1.1$ Å, respectively, and narrow nebular lines, reclassifying both as extremely UV-luminous galaxies. Standard population-synthesis models cannot simultaneously reproduce the strong He II and wind features, whereas models incorporating very massive stars (VMS; $M\gtrsim100\,M_\odot$) with dedicated wind prescriptions can. These models favor a star-formation duration of 2-4 Myr for J1450-0144, with a broader allowed range for J1429-0104, stellar masses of $\log(M_\star/M_\odot)\approx9.2$-$9.9$, and star-formation rates of $\simeq300$-$540\,M_\odot\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$. Under the same VMS wind models, equivalent-width diagnostics imply $M_{\rm up}\gtrsim225\,M_\odot$ for J1429-0104, while J1450-0144 lies beyond even the $M_{\rm up}=475\,M_\odot$ grid. ALMA detects luminous [C II] 158 $μ$m emission in both systems, with $L_{\rm [CII]}\approx0.8$ and $4.1\times10^{9}\,L_\odot$, respectively. J1429-0104 additionally shows bright dust continuum, with both [C II] and dust offset by $\sim5.4$ kpc from its UV emission. These sources demonstrate that VMS can power some of the most UV-luminous galaxies at cosmic dawn and show that source classifications, and hence the inferred demographics of both galaxies and quasars in the crossover regime, need revisiting.

AI.tldr: JWST/NIRSpec and ALMA observations reclassify two M_UV~-23.5 sources (originally classified as faint quasars by SHELLQs at z~6.6-6.8) as extremely UV-luminous star-forming galaxies. The spectra show blue UV continua, strong P Cygni wind profiles, and broad He II emission that standard population-synthesis models cannot reproduce, but models with very massive stars (M>100 M_sun) can. ALMA detects luminous [C II] emission in both, with one source showing dust continuum offset by ~5.4 kpc from its UV emission. This demonstrates VMS can power some of the most UV-luminous galaxies at cosmic dawn and that galaxy/quasar classification in this regime needs revision.
AI.motivation: The extreme bright end of the galaxy UV luminosity function during reionisation is poorly constrained, and source classification at the crossover where galaxy and quasar luminosity functions overlap is ambiguous, affecting inferred demographics of both populations.
AI.method: JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy and ALMA Band-6 observations of two M_UV~-23.5 sources at z=6.627 and z=6.796 originally classified as faint quasars by SHELLQs. Spectral features are compared to population-synthesis models, including those with very massive stars (M>100 M_sun) and dedicated wind prescriptions.
AI.result: Both sources are reclassified as extremely UV-luminous galaxies based on blue UV continua, P Cygni profiles, broad He II emission (EWs 8.8 and 3.7 Å), and narrow nebular lines. VMS wind models reproduce the spectra, implying SF durations of 2-4 Myr (J1450), M_star ~ 10^9.2-10^9.9 M_sun, SFR ~300-540 M_sun/yr, M_up > 225 M_sun (J1429) and beyond 475 M_sun grid (J1450). ALMA detects luminous [C II] (L ~ 0.8 and 4.1x10^9 L_sun), with J1429 showing ~5.4 kpc offsets between [C II]/dust and UV emission.
AI.conclusion: Very massive stars can power some of the most UV-luminous galaxies at cosmic dawn, and source classifications—and therefore inferred galaxy and quasar demographics—in the crossover regime need revisiting.

title: Towards end-to-end Bayesian forward models in global 21-cm cosmology: surrogate modelling and marginalisation of beam uncertainty
comment: 19 pages, 15 figures, 4 tables
summary: Robust statistical inference in global 21-cm cosmology requires end-to-end uncertainty quantification that jointly handles the highly degenerate cosmological signal, foreground emission, and instrumental response. Although electromagnetic simulations capture physical antenna properties in a parametrised way, multi-hour runtimes make their integration within likelihood-based sampling frameworks infeasible. Most existing approaches therefore assume a single precomputed beam, a fragile assumption given our demonstration that realistic mismatches can severely bias the recovered cosmological and foreground parameters. To address this, we present an accelerated and differentiable Bayesian framework that incorporates an informed surrogate representation of chromatic beam uncertainty directly into a forward-modelling pipeline. Treating the physical antenna properties as nuisance quantities, we apply a two-stage decomposition directly to simulated directivity patterns, reducing the instrumental parameterisation by two orders of magnitude while retaining the angular and spectral structure required for accurate beam reconstruction. Exploiting the linearity of the resulting surrogate, we use analytical marginalisation to allow the continuous instrumental uncertainty to be propagated into the final posteriors and Bayesian evidence without directly sampling the beam space. Testing the framework against a suite of unseen beams and cosmological signals, we recover the true inputs at approximately the instrumental-noise level. We further show that, for the uncertainty considered here, as few as 100 electromagnetic simulations are sufficient to construct an effective surrogate, substantially reducing the simulation burden for future analyses. This framework provides a scalable, statistically rigorous route towards hardware-accelerated uncertainty quantification in global 21-cm cosmology.

AI.tldr: The paper presents an accelerated and differentiable Bayesian framework for global 21-cm cosmology that incorporates chromatic beam uncertainty into forward-modelling via a surrogate representation of simulated antenna directivity patterns. The method reduces instrumental parameterization by two orders of magnitude, uses analytical marginalization to propagate continuous instrumental uncertainty into posteriors without directly sampling beam space, and recovers true inputs at approximately instrumental-noise level using as few as 100 electromagnetic simulations.
AI.motivation: Existing approaches assume a single precomputed antenna beam, which is fragile because realistic beam mismatches can severely bias recovered cosmological and foreground parameters. Electromagnetic simulations capture physical antenna properties but have multi-hour runtimes, making them infeasible for integration within likelihood-based sampling frameworks.
AI.method: The framework uses a two-stage decomposition applied directly to simulated directivity patterns to create an informed surrogate representation of chromatic beam uncertainty, treating physical antenna properties as nuisance quantities. It exploits the linearity of the surrogate and applies analytical marginalisation to propagate continuous instrumental uncertainty into final posteriors and Bayesian evidence without directly sampling the beam space.
AI.result: Testing against a suite of unseen beams and cosmological signals, the framework recovers true inputs at approximately the instrumental-noise level. As few as 100 electromagnetic simulations are sufficient to construct an effective surrogate for the uncertainty considered, substantially reducing the simulation burden.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides a scalable, statistically rigorous route towards hardware-accelerated uncertainty quantification in global 21-cm cosmology, jointly handling the highly degenerate cosmological signal, foreground emission, and instrumental response with end-to-end uncertainty propagation.

title: Automated Assignment and Prediction of Molecules in Astronomical Line Surveys Using Machine-Learning-Based Chemical Embeddings
comment: Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal
summary: Modern radio telescopes generate vast amounts of observational data, offering valuable insights into the molecular composition of interstellar sources. Identifying the molecules within these datasets typically involves time-consuming and labor-intensive manual analysis. This paper presents an automated method for assigning molecules in interstellar line surveys. The algorithm operates in two main stages. First, it automatically determines key parameters of the data, including excitation temperature, line width, and source velocity. Next, it assigns the observed spectral peaks by evaluating the spectroscopic match of the molecular candidates along with analyzing their chemical relevance to the interstellar source. The chemical relevance is determined by leveraging machine-learning-based molecular embedding techniques to analyze the regions of chemical space occupied by the observed species. Following the line assignment, this information is then used to generate new molecular candidates that occupy the same regions of chemical space. These newly generated species serve as promising targets for further investigation in the observational data. The algorithm was validated on spectral line surveys of the dark molecular cloud TMC-1 and the star-forming region IRAS 16293-2422B. In both cases, it identified at least 67 molecular species, accounting for over 90 percent of the analyzed line intensity, in 17 minutes or less while maintaining a high level of accuracy.

AI.tldr: This paper presents an automated two-stage algorithm for assigning molecules in interstellar line surveys. The algorithm first determines key data parameters (excitation temperature, line width, source velocity) and then assigns spectral peaks by evaluating spectroscopic match combined with machine-learning-based chemical relevance. It also generates new molecular candidates occupying the same chemical space regions. Validated on TMC-1 and IRAS 16293-2422B, it identified at least 67 molecular species covering over 90% of line intensity in 17 minutes or less with high accuracy.
AI.motivation: Modern radio telescopes generate vast amounts of observational data on interstellar molecular composition, but identifying molecules in these datasets typically requires time-consuming and labor-intensive manual analysis. An automated method is needed to accelerate molecular identification in interstellar line surveys.
AI.method: The algorithm operates in two stages: (1) automatic determination of key data parameters including excitation temperature, line width, and source velocity; (2) spectral peak assignment by evaluating spectroscopic match of molecular candidates combined with machine-learning-based molecular embedding analysis of chemical space relevance. The chemical information is then used to generate new molecular candidates occupying the same chemical space regions for further investigation.
AI.result: Validated on spectral line surveys of TMC-1 (dark molecular cloud) and IRAS 16293-2422B (star-forming region). The algorithm identified at least 67 molecular species in each case, accounting for over 90% of the analyzed line intensity, completing the analysis in 17 minutes or less while maintaining high accuracy.
AI.conclusion: The automated algorithm successfully accelerates molecular assignment in interstellar line surveys, achieving high accuracy and coverage in a fraction of the time required for manual analysis, while also proposing new molecular candidates for further observational investigation.

title: Dipolar power asymmetry in wide-angle correlations of galaxy density, velocity and ellipticity
comment: 22 pages, 3 figures
summary: The large-scale structure of the universe has the potential to probe anomalies suggested by observations of the cosmic microwave background. In this work, we focus on a position-dependent dipolar modulation of the primordial power spectrum and develop a full-sky formalism for computing correlation functions of galaxy density, velocity and ellipticity. By comparing the correlation functions obtained with and without the plane-parallel approximation, we show that wide-angle corrections become non-negligible for opening angles $Θ\gtrsim 30^\circ$. Our results demonstrate that wide-angle corrections must be taken into account when testing the dipolar modulation with future large-scale structure surveys.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a full-sky formalism for computing correlation functions of galaxy density, velocity and ellipticity to probe a position-dependent dipolar modulation of the primordial power spectrum, demonstrating that wide-angle corrections become non-negligible for opening angles greater than ~30 degrees and must be included when testing dipolar modulation with future large-scale structure surveys.
AI.motivation: The large-scale structure of the universe can probe anomalies suggested by observations of the cosmic microwave background, specifically a position-dependent dipolar modulation of the primordial power spectrum.
AI.method: The authors develop a full-sky formalism to compute correlation functions of galaxy density, velocity, and ellipticity, and compare results with and without the plane-parallel approximation to assess the impact of wide-angle corrections.
AI.result: Wide-angle corrections become non-negligible for opening angles Θ ≳ 30°, and must be taken into account when testing dipolar modulation with future large-scale structure surveys.
AI.conclusion: Wide-angle corrections are necessary for accurate testing of dipolar modulation signals using future large-scale structure observations.

title: Accretion of AGN Stars under Influence of Disk Geometry II: The Adiabatic Regime and Runaway Collapse Induced by Self-gravity
comment: Accepted to ApJ
summary:
Accretion onto massive stars embedded in Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN) disks around supermassive black holes (SMBHs) is regulated to the stellar Eddington rate in the fast-diffusion or radiatively-efficient limit, $c/τ> c_s$, where $τ$ is the optical depth of the accretion flow and $c_s$ the sound speed. However, when the ambient density is sufficiently high, the opposite slow-diffusion limit applies. In this regime, accretion proceeds quasi-adiabatically and forms a hydrostatic circumstellar envelope (CSE) that stalls further mass inflow in the absence of self-gravity. We perform 3D hydrodynamic simulations in the adiabatic limit to investigate the structure and evolution of such envelopes. For low thermal mass ratios, $q_{\rm th} \equiv M_\star/M_{\rm th}$ where $M_{\rm th}=c_s^3/(GΩ)$ is the thermal mass, the CSE boundary smoothly matches the ambient disk entropy and density without forming a shock.
  In contrast, when $q_{\rm th} \gg 1$, a strong shock develops at the envelope boundary, substantially increasing the entropy of the envelope and thereby regulating its structure and mass, $M_{\rm env}$. In marginally self-gravitating disks with Toomre parameter $Q \sim 1$, we find that at sufficiently large $q_{\rm th}$ the envelope mass satisfies $M_{\rm env}/M_\star \gtrsim 1$. This condition is equivalent to stating that the post-shock material entering the envelope possesses lower radiation entropy than the characteristic stellar value, which triggers dynamical runaway growth on a dynamical timescale once envelope self-gravity is included in our simulations. In realistic AGN disk environments with SMBH mass $\sim 10^8M_\odot$, runaway may occur close to the minimum self-gravitating radii and produce supermassive stars of $\sim 10^5M_\odot$.

AI.tldr: This paper uses 3D hydrodynamic simulations to study accretion onto massive stars embedded in AGN disks. In the slow-diffusion (quasi-adiabatic) limit, a hydrostatic circumstellar envelope forms around the star. For low thermal mass ratios (q_th), the envelope smoothly matches the ambient disk, but for q_th >> 1, a strong shock develops, increasing envelope entropy. In marginally self-gravitating disks (Q~1), large q_th leads to envelope mass exceeding the stellar mass, triggering dynamical runaway growth when self-gravity is included. In realistic AGN disks around 10^8 M_sun SMBHs, this can produce supermassive stars of ~10^5 M_sun near the minimum self-gravitating radii.
AI.motivation: To understand how massive stars embedded in AGN disks accrete matter when the ambient density is high enough that the slow-diffusion (adiabatic) limit applies, rather than the fast-diffusion case where accretion is regulated to the stellar Eddington rate. This regime is important for understanding the formation of supermassive stars from AGN disk environments.
AI.method: 3D hydrodynamic simulations in the adiabatic limit, investigating the structure and evolution of circumstellar envelopes formed during accretion onto stars embedded in AGN disks. The study examines envelope structure as a function of thermal mass ratio q_th = M_star/M_th and includes self-gravity in simulations to study dynamical runaway growth.
AI.result: Two distinct regimes are found: for low q_th, the CSE boundary smoothly matches the ambient disk without a shock; for q_th >> 1, a strong shock develops at the envelope boundary, increasing entropy and regulating envelope structure and mass. In marginally self-gravitating disks (Q~1), sufficiently large q_th yields M_env/M_star >= 1, triggering dynamical runaway growth once self-gravity is included. In realistic AGN disks with 10^8 M_sun SMBHs, runaway can produce supermassive stars of ~10^5 M_sun near the minimum self-gravitating radii.
AI.conclusion: Accretion onto massive stars in dense AGN disk environments can proceed via quasi-adiabatic envelope formation, where shock-mediated entropy enhancement and envelope self-gravity can trigger dynamical runaway growth. This mechanism may naturally produce supermassive stars of ~10^5 M_sun in realistic AGN disks around massive SMBHs.

title: The MAGPI Survey: Emission Line Products Data Release and the Role of Spectroscopic Aperture Covering Fraction on the Balmer Decrement-Stellar Mass Relation
comment: 25 pages, 16 figures, 9 tables. These data products are being hosted on Data Central (https://docs.datacentral.org.au/magpi/). They are also available as .zip files for download here (https://cloud.datacentral.org.au/teamdata/MAGPI/public/). Accepted for publication in MNRAS
summary: The Middle Ages Galaxy Properties with Integral field spectroscopy (MAGPI) survey is a Large Program on the European Southern Observatory Very Large Telescope using the MUSE instrument. This paper presents the data release for the MAGPI emission line products and includes emission line maps for 836 galaxies at $0.05\leq z_\mathrm{spec}\leq 0.424$ ($\mathrm{H}α$-window) and aperture-based emission line measurements for 2,607 galaxies at $0.05\leq z_\mathrm{spec}\leq 1.50$ (upper bound is [OII] cut-off), both based on the GIST software, for all 56 MAGPI fields. We use these data to examine dust attenuation, which represents a major source of uncertainty in the derived properties of galaxies that are critical to constrain models of galaxy evolution. We examine the role that the spectroscopic aperture covering fraction ($f_c$) has on the relationship between the Balmer decrement ($\mathrm{BD}=F(\mathrm{H}α)/F(\mathrm{H}β)$; a common proxy for dust attenuation) and the total stellar mass ($M_\star$). Several studies have suggested that the BD-$M_\star$ relation may be redshift invariant; however, the compared surveys often have different $f_c$ due to their differing fibre or slit sizes that can cause systematic offsets. Our results indicate that $f_c$ has a significant impact on this relationship, due to galaxies having negative BD radial gradients, which are more negative for more massive galaxies at $z\lesssim0.4$. Comparing spectroscopic surveys with $\left<f_c\right> \gtrsim 0.5$, we find that the BD-$M_\star$ relation shows a preference for redshift evolution and is roughly consistent with the behaviour of UV stellar continuum attenuation redshift evolution ($A_\mathrm{FUV}$-$z$), with the average dust attenuation in galaxies peaking at $z\sim1.2$ and decreasing at lower and higher redshifts.

AI.tldr: The MAGPI survey data release presents emission line maps for 836 galaxies and aperture-based measurements for 2,607 galaxies using MUSE integral field spectroscopy. The study examines how the spectroscopic aperture covering fraction affects the Balmer decrement–stellar mass relation, finding that covering fraction significantly biases this relationship. When controlling for covering fraction, the BD-M* relation shows redshift evolution consistent with UV stellar continuum attenuation, peaking at z~1.2.
AI.motivation: Dust attenuation is a major source of uncertainty in derived galaxy properties crucial for constraining galaxy evolution models. Previous studies suggested the Balmer decrement–stellar mass relation might be redshift invariant, but comparisons across surveys are confounded by differing fibre/slit sizes (aperture covering fractions) that can cause systematic offsets. The authors aim to quantify the impact of aperture covering fraction and reassess the true redshift evolution of dust attenuation.
AI.method: The study uses MAGPI data from MUSE on the VLT, processing emission line data with the GIST software. They produce emission line maps for 836 galaxies (Hα-window) and aperture-based measurements for 2,607 galaxies, spanning z~0.05-1.50. They analyze the Balmer decrement (Hα/Hβ) as a dust attenuation proxy, examining its relation to stellar mass while accounting for the spectroscopic aperture covering fraction (fc). They compare their results with other surveys, restricting comparisons to those with mean fc ≳ 0.5.
AI.result: The aperture covering fraction significantly impacts the BD-M* relation because galaxies exhibit negative BD radial gradients, which are more pronounced for more massive galaxies at z≲0.4. When comparing surveys with high covering fractions (mean fc ≳ 0.5), the BD-M* relation shows a preference for redshift evolution rather than invariance. The evolution is roughly consistent with UV stellar continuum attenuation evolution (AFUV-z), with average dust attenuation peaking at z~1.2 and decreasing at both lower and higher redshifts.
AI.conclusion: The BD-M* relation is not redshift invariant once aperture effects are properly accounted for. Dust attenuation evolves with redshift, peaking around z~1.2. Aperture covering fraction must be carefully considered when comparing dust attenuation measurements across different spectroscopic surveys, as systematic offsets due to differing fibre/slit sizes can bias conclusions about redshift evolution.

title: Continuum Variability in AGN: Evidence for Systematically Suppressed Fluctuations in the BAL Population
comment: Accepted for publication in A&A
summary: We aim to compare the flux variability of Broad Absorption Line quasars (BAL) to non-BAL quasars, controlling for black hole parameters to inform models concerning the generation of the BAL phenomenon. Using SDSS DR16 and ZTF $g$- and $r$-band light curves, we select quasars with $1.57 \leq z \leq 2.00$ and $18.5 \leq rmag \leq 19.8$. This redshift range ensures that the $g$-band covers the C IV emission line (and trough in BALs) while the $r$-band probes continuum variability, and allows black hole mass (MBH) estimates via Mg II. We quantify variability using excess variance and damped random walk (DRW) parameters ($σ_{\mathrm{DRW}}$, $τ_{\mathrm{DRW}}$). We also compared the DRW metrics in bins of MBH and Eddington ratio (REdd) to isolate the influence of the BAL phenomenon in objects with the same physical properties. Excess variance and $σ_{\mathrm{DRW}}$ are consistently smaller for BALs, confirming lower long-term variability, while the $g$-band exhibits higher variability than the $r$-band across both populations. These differences persist in fixed bins of MBH and REdd, indicating that the suppressed variability in BALs is not simply driven by differences in these properties between BAL and non-BAL samples. These results show that BAL quasars are systematically less variable than non-BAL quasars in both bands, confirming that this suppression is an intrinsic feature of the continuum rather than an effect of emission or absorption line contamination. The samples could be made to agree if BAL MBH values were systematically overestimated by a factor $\gtrsim 4$, implying a significantly higher REdd. Alternatively, the lower variability in BALs can be related to their lower X-ray luminosities, or to significant nuclear obscuration, if the inner part of the accretion disc were more obscured in BALs and more variable than the rest of the disc.

AI.tldr: This paper compares the flux variability of Broad Absorption Line (BAL) quasars to non-BAL quasars using SDSS DR16 and ZTF light curves, controlling for black hole mass and Eddington ratio. BALs show consistently lower variability (excess variance and DRW σ) in both g- and r-bands, even in matched physical property bins, indicating the suppression is an intrinsic feature of the continuum. Possible explanations include overestimated BAL black hole masses by a factor ≳4, lower X-ray luminosities, or nuclear obscuration of the inner accretion disc.
AI.motivation: To test models of the BAL phenomenon by comparing flux variability between BAL and non-BAL quasars while controlling for black hole parameters, in order to determine whether reduced variability in BALs is intrinsic or due to selection effects, line contamination, or physical property differences.
AI.method: Select quasars with 1.57 ≤ z ≤ 2.00 and 18.5 ≤ rmag ≤ 19.8 from SDSS DR16 and ZTF. Use the g-band to probe the C IV line region (and trough in BALs) and r-band for continuum variability. Estimate black hole masses via Mg II. Quantify variability using excess variance and damped random walk (DRW) parameters (σ_DRW, τ_DRW), comparing in bins of black hole mass and Eddington ratio.
AI.result: BALs show consistently smaller excess variance and σ_DRW in both bands, confirming lower long-term variability. The g-band shows higher variability than the r-band in both populations. Differences persist even when binning by black hole mass and Eddington ratio, ruling out these properties as the sole drivers. The suppression is intrinsic to the continuum, not from line contamination.
AI.conclusion: BAL quasars are systematically less variable than non-BAL quasars, an intrinsic continuum property. This could be reconciled if BAL black hole masses were overestimated by ≳4× (implying higher Eddington ratios), or explained by lower X-ray luminosities in BALs, or by nuclear obscuration where the inner, more variable part of the accretion disc is hidden.

title: Inferring the Dark from the Observable: Estimating Halo Masses Using Galaxy Properties
comment: 22 pages, 19 figures (including appendices), comments welcome
summary: The formation and evolution of galaxies are interconnected with that of their host halos. Given this closely related evolutionary history, it should follow that galaxy properties are correlated with their host halo mass. Previous works have shown that star formation rates of galaxies in cluster halos differ systematically from those in field halos, suggesting that host halo mass plays a significant role in the history of galaxy evolution. Here, we examine the correlations between observable galaxy properties - such as stellar mass, star formation rate, half-stellar radius, $r-$band magnitude, and color - and the underlying host halo mass of galaxies. Central galaxy observables are used to probe host halo mass, while satellite galaxy properties are used to estimate subhalo mass. We perform this analysis using random forest, ordinary least squares (OLS), and symbolic regression. Random forest regression can assess the relative significance of different observable galaxy properties, while OLS and symbolic regression can quantify their relationship with the host halo mass. Our results show that gas mass is generally the most significant property in central galaxies of all halo mass ranges, followed by stellar mass and observed $r-$band magnitude. Adding parameters such as the colour and magnitude of galaxies improves host halo mass estimations compared to standard stellar-to-halo mass relations. These results show that halo mass likely has a multi-dimensional dependence on galaxy properties and open the avenue of finding a simple way to constrain halo mass based on what is directly observable in galaxy surveys. Finding the observables that have the strongest correlation with halo mass can also motivate future surveys on which areas to concentrate in detail.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates correlations between observable galaxy properties (stellar mass, star formation rate, half-stellar radius, r-band magnitude, color) and host halo mass using random forest, OLS, and symbolic regression. Gas mass is the most significant predictor of halo mass across all mass ranges, followed by stellar mass and r-band magnitude. The authors find halo mass depends multi-dimensionally on galaxy properties, and adding color/magnitude improves halo mass estimation over standard stellar-to-halo mass relations.
AI.motivation: Galaxy formation and evolution are tightly linked to their host halos, and previous work shows galaxy properties in cluster vs. field halos differ systematically. Understanding which observable galaxy properties best correlate with halo mass could provide simple ways to constrain halo mass from surveys and guide future observational priorities.
AI.method: The authors use three regression techniques: (1) random forest regression to assess relative importance of observable galaxy properties, (2) ordinary least squares (OLS), and (3) symbolic regression, both used to quantify relationships between observables and host halo mass. Central galaxy observables probe host halo mass while satellite properties estimate subhalo mass.
AI.result: Gas mass is the most significant property for central galaxies across all halo mass ranges, followed by stellar mass and observed r-band magnitude. Including color and magnitude improves host halo mass estimation compared to standard stellar-to-halo mass relations, indicating a multi-dimensional dependence of halo mass on galaxy properties.
AI.conclusion: Halo mass has a multi-dimensional dependence on observable galaxy properties beyond stellar mass alone. The identified key observables can enable simple estimation of halo mass from survey data and can inform future surveys on which properties to prioritize observing in detail.

title: Dynamics of tidal dwarf galaxies in the system Arp 72
comment: Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics (A&A). 19 pages, 17 figures
summary: Some interactions between galaxies produce tidal tails primarily composed of material from their disks. Within these tails, concentrations of gas and stars can form, resembling dwarf galaxies. These tidal objects often begin to form stars and become dynamically independent of their parent galaxies, leading to their classification as Tidal Dwarf Galaxies (TDGs). By definition, TDGs should consist solely of baryonic material, with a negligible dark matter fraction. In this study, we analyze the dynamics of two TDGs in the Arp 72 system using high-resolution Hα observations obtained with the MEGARA multi-spectrograph at the GTC (Gran Telescopio Canarias) and neutral hydrogen (HI) data from the GMRT (Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope). The HI data were also used to determine the gas mass. We derived the rotation curves and velocity dispersion from the kinematic data, which allowed us to estimate the dynamical mass of the systems. The TDGs were modeled through 3D fitting as rotating disks with additional pressure support, assuming a mass distribution following an exponential law. The gas mass was combined with the stellar mass to determine the total baryonic mass. Under specific dynamical considerations, we established the relationship between the dynamical mass and the baryonic mass. Additionally, we used the pressure-support corrected circular velocity to compare the behavior of TDGs in the context of the baryonic Tully-Fisher relation (BTFR) with the literature, showing how detached TDGs fall off the relation. The two studied objects are consistent with the expected properties of a TDG.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes the dynamics of two Tidal Dwarf Galaxies (TDGs) in the Arp 72 system using high-resolution Hα observations from MEGARA at GTC and HI data from GMRT. The authors derive rotation curves, velocity dispersions, dynamical and baryonic masses via 3D rotating disk modeling with pressure support, and compare the TDGs against the baryonic Tully-Fisher relation, finding them consistent with expected TDG properties and showing detached TDGs fall off the BTFR.
AI.motivation: Tidal Dwarf Galaxies are unique objects formed from galaxy interactions, and by definition should be purely baryonic with negligible dark matter. Testing whether observed tidal objects match this expectation requires precise kinematic and dynamical analysis, which motivates this detailed study of two candidate TDGs in the Arp 72 system.
AI.method: The study uses high-resolution Hα emission data from the MEGARA spectrograph at GTC and HI data from GMRT. Rotation curves and velocity dispersions were derived from kinematics to estimate dynamical masses. TDGs were modeled via 3D fitting as rotating exponential disks with pressure support. Gas mass from HI data was combined with stellar mass for total baryonic mass, and pressure-support corrected circular velocities were used for comparison with the baryonic Tully-Fisher relation.
AI.result: The relationship between dynamical and baryonic mass was established under specific dynamical considerations. The two TDG candidates, when placed in the baryonic Tully-Fisher relation context, exhibit a fall-off consistent with detached TDGs. Both objects are confirmed to have properties consistent with expected TDG characteristics.
AI.conclusion: The two studied objects in the Arp 72 system satisfy the expected properties of Tidal Dwarf Galaxies, and their deviation from the baryonic Tully-Fisher relation further supports the interpretation that detached TDGs are dark-matter-free, purely baryonic systems formed from tidal interactions.

title: A model for the enhanced production rate of early-type hypervelocity stars in the Galactic halo
comment: 11 Pages, 5 figures, accepted for publication in ApJL
summary: About twenty late B-type hypervelocity stars (HVSs) traveling faster than the Galactic escape velocity have been discovered in the Galactic halo, many of which were ejected from the Galactic center (GC). Recently, we have advocated that these HVSs most likely formed in the nuclear star cluster (NSC) $150$--$500\, \rm{Myr}$ ago and were predominantly ejected via the gravitational slingshot of a past intermediate-mass black hole (IMBH) orbiting the supermassive black hole (SMBH) Sgr~A$^{*}$. Here we explore the constraints of the production rate of young HVSs on the star formation region of the NSC. We propose that the young HVS progenitors are born in a lopsided eccentric disk that is comparable in radius to the NSC. By numerically tracking the orbital evolution of disk stars, we find that they undergo rapid angular momentum relaxation at formation due to eccentric disk instability, and that their slingshot interactions with the SMBH-IMBH binary at distances $\simeq 100\, \rm{au}$ produce HVSs at a rate of $10^{-5}$--$10^{-4}\, \rm{yr}^{-1}$. The rate is expected to trace the disk formation history, increasing with the accumulation of disk stars and dropping rapidly after the star formation stopped at $150\, \rm{Myr}$ ago. The rate is consistent with the observation and orders of magnitude higher than that expected for an old relaxed population in the literature, enhanced due to the gravitational torque from the non-spherical GC potential and radial velocity anisotropies of the disk stars. Our results imply that young HVSs should have a distinct radial and angular distribution from old ones.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes that young late B-type hypervelocity stars (HVSs) in the Galactic halo were produced by slingshot ejection from an intermediate-mass black hole (IMBH) orbiting Sgr A*, with progenitors born in a lopsided eccentric nuclear star cluster disk. Simulations show disk instability drives rapid angular momentum relaxation, yielding HVS production rates of 10^-5–10^-4 yr^-1 consistent with observations, implying distinct spatial distributions between young and old HVSs.
AI.motivation: To constrain the star formation region of the Galactic nuclear star cluster (NSC) by explaining the production rate of young HVSs ejected via a past IMBH interacting with the SMBH Sgr A*.
AI.method: The authors numerically track the orbital evolution of disk stars in a lopsided eccentric disk comparable in radius to the NSC, modeling eccentric disk instability-driven angular momentum relaxation and slingshot interactions with the SMBH-IMBH binary at ~100 AU distances.
AI.result: The model produces HVSs at a rate of 10^-5–10^-4 yr^-1, consistent with observation and orders of magnitude higher than expected for an old relaxed population. The rate traces disk formation history, increasing with disk star accumulation and dropping after star formation ceased 150 Myr ago.
AI.conclusion: Young HVSs should have a distinct radial and angular distribution from old HVSs, and their production is enhanced by gravitational torque from the non-spherical GC potential and radial velocity anisotropies of disk stars.

title: Beyond Idealized PAHs: Infrared Signatures of Carbon-Chain Defects from Shock Synthesis
summary: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) are widely recognized as carriers of the aromatic infrared bands (AIBs). However, most spectral models rely on idealized structures that fail to capture the energetic environments of interstellar PAH formation. This work investigates the infrared (IR) signatures of PAHs formed under shock conditions and explores whether produced defective structures can explain observational features unpredicted by standard, idealized models. We combine two-stage reactive molecular dynamics simulations of PAH formation via condensation and shock processing with density functional theory spectral calculations, and compare our theoretical results with James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) observations of NGC 7023 and MRK 1066. Shock processing produces PAHs featuring fullerene-like carbon skeletons and linear carbon-chain attachments. These structural defects yield distinct IR signatures, including prominent carbon-chain stretching features at 4.6-5.5 micron that is absent in ideal PAHs, and significantly enhanced out-of-plane skeletal modes in the 14.5-20 micron regime. Our findings attribute the observed 5.2 micron band in NGC 7023 and MRK 1066 to carbon-chain vibrations and the 15-18 micron emission to curved skeletal modes, providing observational support for the prevalence of defective, shock-formed PAHs in the interstellar medium.

AI.tldr: This work combines reactive molecular dynamics simulations and DFT spectral calculations to study IR signatures of PAHs formed under shock conditions. Shock-formed PAHs exhibit fullerene-like skeletons and carbon-chain attachments producing distinct IR features at 4.6-5.5 and 14.5-20 micron, explaining JWST observations of NGC 7023 and MRK 1066 that standard idealized PAH models cannot predict.
AI.motivation: Standard PAH spectral models rely on idealized structures that fail to capture the energetic environments of interstellar PAH formation, leaving observational features unexplained.
AI.method: Two-stage reactive molecular dynamics simulations of PAH formation via condensation and shock processing, combined with density functional theory spectral calculations, compared against JWST observations of NGC 7023 and MRK 1066.
AI.result: Shock processing produces PAHs with fullerene-like carbon skeletons and linear carbon-chain attachments, yielding distinct IR features: carbon-chain stretching at 4.6-5.5 micron absent in ideal PAHs, and enhanced out-of-plane skeletal modes at 14.5-20 micron. The observed 5.2 micron band and 15-18 micron emission are attributed to these defective structures.
AI.conclusion: The findings provide observational support for the prevalence of defective, shock-formed PAHs in the interstellar medium, offering an explanation for AIB features unpredicted by idealized models.

title: Kinematics and Dynamics of the Open Cluster NGC 2302
comment: 10 pages, 13 figures, accepted for publication in JKAS
summary: Open clusters are ideal observational testbeds to understand the dynamics of stellar systems. We present a dynamical study of the young open cluster NGC 2302. The latest Gaia data and $UBVIJHK_s$ photometric data are used in this study. A total of 117 stars are selected as the genuine members using the Gaia data. This cluster is, on average, reddened by $<E(B-V)> = 0.24 \pm 0.06$ (s.d.). The ratio of total-to-selective extinction ($R_V$) in the direction of NGC 2302 is $2.8 \pm 0.1$. The cluster distance is determined to be $1.16 \pm 0.08$ kpc using Gaia parallaxes. Theoretical isochrone fitting for $Z = 0.008$ on color-magnitude diagrams yields an age of $80 \pm 20$ Myr. The relative proper motions of individual members show no significant radial expansion or contraction. NGC 2302 contains a total stellar mass of $333 \pm 48 M_{\odot}$. The one-dimensional velocity dispersion is approximately 0.26 km s$^{-1}$, which is comparable to the viral velocity dispersion of 0.27 km s$^{-1}$ derived from its total mass. Its relaxation time is estimated to be approximately 90 Myr, which is similar to the age of the cluster within the uncertainty in age estimation. Finally, we report a pattern of mass segregation in the radial distribution of stellar masses. Our results suggest that NGC 2302 is virialized and currently approaching a state of dynamical relaxation. However, because no definitive evidence of kinetic energy equipartition is found, the possibility of the in-situ formation of high-mass stars within the central region should be carefully considered.

AI.tldr: A dynamical study of the young open cluster NGC 2302 using Gaia data and UBVIJHKs photometry identifies 117 genuine members, determines fundamental parameters (distance ~1.16 kpc, age ~80 Myr, mass ~333 M☉, extinction E(B-V)=0.24), and finds the cluster is virialized and approaching dynamical relaxation with possible mass segregation, though no definitive kinetic energy equipartition is found.
AI.motivation: Open clusters serve as ideal observational testbeds for understanding stellar system dynamics. This study aims to characterize the dynamical state of the young open cluster NGC 2302, determining whether it is virialized, relaxed, and exhibiting mass segregation.
AI.method: The study uses Gaia astrometric data combined with UBVIJHKs photometric observations. Membership selection identifies 117 genuine cluster members from Gaia data. Key dynamical and physical parameters are derived including reddening, total-to-selective extinction ratio (R_V), distance from Gaia parallaxes, age from isochrone fitting (Z=0.008), stellar mass, velocity dispersion, relaxation time, and mass segregation analysis of radial mass distribution.
AI.result: The cluster has E(B-V)=0.24±0.06, R_V=2.8±0.1, distance=1.16±0.08 kpc, age=80±20 Myr, and total mass=333±48 M☉. The 1D velocity dispersion (0.26 km/s) matches the virial velocity dispersion (0.27 km/s). Relaxation time (~90 Myr) is similar to the cluster age. No significant radial expansion/contraction in proper motions, but mass segregation is present in the radial stellar mass distribution.
AI.conclusion: NGC 2302 appears virialized and approaching a state of dynamical relaxation. However, given the lack of definitive kinetic energy equipartition evidence, the in-situ formation of high-mass stars in the central region should be considered as a plausible alternative explanation for the observed mass segregation.

title: Hector Galaxy Survey: Falling in Between - Infalling Galaxies in the Midst of the Abell 3667 Merger
comment: 22 pages, 9 figures, 1 table. Accepted for publication in Publications of the Astronomical Society of Australia (PASA). The abstract has been abridged due to the arXiv's character limit
summary: Whether cluster mergers enhance ram pressure stripping (RPS) and accelerate member galaxy evolution remains an open question. Here, we investigate galaxy populations in the nearby merging cluster Abell 3667 ($z\simeq0.0553$) using spatially resolved data from the Hector Galaxy Survey. We define an RPS sample combining Hector-selected galaxies with ionised gas disturbances (e.g., asymmetric tails or truncated disks) and supplementary, optically identified jellyfish galaxies lacking Hector data. Most of the RPS sample ($\sim 71^{+10}_{-7}\%$; 20/28) lies within $R_{200}$, where the merger impact is greater. Most asymmetric galaxies ($\sim 73^{+14}_{-8}\%$; 11/15), especially those with extreme RPS signatures, are concentrated in the inner cluster ($R \lesssim 0.6\, R_{200}$), along the merger axis between two shock-tracing radio relics. These central asymmetric galaxies show two spatial and kinematic groups: one at the North-West (NW) subcluster, downstream of its radio relic in a region of high-velocity intracluster medium (ICM) bulk motion, with blueshifted line-of-sight velocities; and a mostly redshifted population near the main cluster (MC), which also shows a turbulent ICM. Despite their projected association with the MC core and NW substructure, both samples' velocities indicate they are not bound to them. Tail orientations give insight into orbital histories: NW tails point away from the cluster centre and often align with the merger axis, suggesting merger-driven stripping, while MC tails show neither pattern clearly. Tails are broadly westward, with MC tails tracing due west and NW tails shifted northwest, pointing to two distinct filamentary accretion events for the NW and MC populations. Together, our results indicate enhanced RPS in the heart of A3667, driven mainly by infalling galaxies accreted along nearby filaments interacting with the merger-driven turbulent environment.

AI.tldr: This study of the nearby merging cluster Abell 3667 using Hector Galaxy Survey data finds that ram pressure stripping (RPS) is enhanced in the cluster core, with most RPS galaxies located within R200 and concentrated along the merger axis between two radio relics, suggesting merger-driven stripping from filament-infalling galaxies interacting with turbulent ICM.
AI.motivation: To determine whether cluster mergers enhance ram pressure stripping and accelerate member galaxy evolution, which remains an unresolved question in galaxy evolution studies.
AI.method: Combined spatially resolved Hector Galaxy Survey data (identifying galaxies with ionised gas disturbances like asymmetric tails or truncated disks) with optically identified jellyfish galaxies lacking Hector data to define an RPS sample. Analyzed spatial distributions, line-of-sight kinematics, and tail orientations relative to the cluster structure, merger axis, and radio relics.
AI.result: ~71% of RPS galaxies lie within R200, with asymmetric galaxies (especially extreme RPS cases) concentrated at R ≲ 0.6 R200 along the merger axis between two radio relics. Two spatial/kinematic groups emerge: a blueshifted NW subcluster population downstream of its relic in high-velocity ICM bulk motion, and a mostly redshifted main cluster population in turbulent ICM. Neither population is bound to their projected host structures. NW tails point away from the cluster centre and align with the merger axis, while MC tails are broadly westward, indicating two distinct filamentary accretion events.
AI.conclusion: Ram pressure stripping is enhanced in the core of A3667, driven primarily by infalling galaxies accreted along nearby filaments interacting with the merger-driven turbulent intracluster medium.

title: The Total and Polarized Radio Emission from the Innermost Jets of a High-Redshift Quasar and a Candidate at Parsec-Scale Resolution
comment: 17 pages, 3 figures, accepted for publication in MDPI Universe
summary: High-frequency very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) polarimetry probes synchrotron-emitting plasma closer to the central engines of radio-loud active galactic nuclei (AGNs), but observations above 43 GHz are technically demanding. We present 22-GHz European VLBI Network observations of the $z=4.31$ quasar J1510+5702 and J1606+3124, whose published spectroscopic redshift, $z=4.56$, is uncertain; a photometric estimate gives $z_{\rm phot}=0.9\pm0.1$. For the published $z>4$ redshifts, 22 GHz corresponds to rest-frame frequencies above 118 GHz. Polarized emission is detected in J1510+5702, and a low-level polarized signal is recovered from the brightest feature of J1606+3124. Adopting $z=4.56$, that feature has a brightness temperature of $T_{\mathrm{b,VLBI}}=(7.4\pm0.8)\cdot10^{10}$ K, allowing a mildly Doppler-boosted interpretation, while the young compact-source scenario also remains viable. The core of J1510+5702 has $T_{\mathrm{b,VLBI}}=(1.08\pm0.15) \cdot10^{12}$ K, implying a Doppler factor of ${\sim}22$ under the equipartition assumption. This component has a ${\sim}3.5$ % fractional polarization. These observations show that cm-wavelength VLBI can access rest-frame millimeter-band polarization in bright $z>4$ jets.

AI.tldr: 22-GHz EVN observations of two high-redshift quasars (J1510+5702 at z=4.31 and J1606+3124 at z=4.56/0.9) reveal polarized emission and brightness temperatures implying relativistic Doppler boosting in their jets, demonstrating that cm-wavelength VLBI can probe rest-frame mm-band polarization in z>4 radio-loud AGNs.
AI.motivation: High-frequency VLBI polarimetry probes synchrotron-emitting plasma near AGN central engines, but observations above 43 GHz are technically demanding. The authors aim to demonstrate that cm-wavelength VLBI can access rest-frame mm-band polarization in high-redshift (z>4) jets, which would provide an observationally cheaper avenue to study sub-pc scale jet physics.
AI.method: The authors performed 22-GHz European VLBI Network (EVN) polarimetric observations of two high-redshift quasars, J1510+5702 (z=4.31) and J1606+3124 (published z=4.56 but photometric z~0.9). They measured polarized flux, brightness temperatures, and fractional polarization from VLBI imaging of the jet components.
AI.result: Polarized emission is detected in J1510+5702 with ~3.5% fractional polarization and a core brightness temperature of 1.08e12 K, implying a Doppler factor of ~22 under equipartition. A low-level polarized signal is recovered in J1606+3124's brightest feature, with T_b = 7.4e10 K at z=4.56, allowing a mildly Doppler-boosted interpretation.
AI.conclusion: cm-wavelength VLBI can effectively access rest-frame millimeter-band polarization in bright z>4 jets, providing a viable alternative to technically demanding high-frequency observations for probing jet physics at early cosmic epochs.

title: Size-Mass Relation Shows Its Colours: Contrasting Physical Imprints of Galaxy Evolution in Rest-Frame UV and Optical
comment: 34 pages, 2 figures, 2 tables. Invited review to appear in the Galaxies special issue on Unveiling the Structural Properties of Galaxies Using Contemporary Wide-Field Surveys
summary: The galaxy size-mass relation (SMR) is a key scaling relation used to constrain the physical processes that build galaxy structure, yet it is almost always measured in a single rest-frame optical band, where the light traces the bulk of the old stellar mass. Tracing younger populations with flux-weighted ages of ~100-500 Myr and low-metallicity stars, the rest-frame near-ultraviolet opens a new stellar window on this scaling relation. Because each process redistributes the light of young and old stars differently, the same mechanism shifts the slope and zero point of the SMR by different amounts in the two wavelength regimes. Here we review and synthesize the effects of main physical processes on the form of the SMR for star-forming and quiescent galaxies in the rest-UV and optical. For each process, we start from its underlying physics, the galaxy stellar masses it affects, and the light it adds/removes/rearranges, anchoring the predictions to observations and simulations. We validate the predicted imprints with forward Monte Carlo modelling. The two-wavelength view breaks several degeneracies that single-band analyses cannot, most notably between minor mergers, dry major mergers, and adiabatic expansion. These results motivate joint rest-UV and optical SMR measurements with current and upcoming wide-field imaging surveys.

AI.tldr: This paper reviews and synthesizes the effects of key physical processes on the galaxy size-mass relation (SMR) measured in both the rest-frame near-ultraviolet and optical bands. Using observations, simulations, and forward Monte Carlo modelling, the authors show that the two-wavelength view breaks degeneracies—particularly between minor mergers, dry major mergers, and adiabatic expansion—that single-band analyses cannot resolve.
AI.motivation: The SMR is normally measured in a single rest-frame optical band tracing old stellar mass. Using the rest-frame near-UV, which traces younger (~100-500 Myr) and low-metallicity stellar populations, opens a new window. Because physical processes redistribute young and old stellar light differently, a two-wavelength analysis can break degeneracies that single-band measurements cannot.
AI.method: The authors synthesize the physical effects of galaxy formation processes on the SMR in both rest-UV and optical bands for star-forming and quiescent galaxies. For each process, they trace its underlying physics, affected stellar masses, and the light it adds/removes/rearranges, anchoring predictions to observations and simulations, then validate predicted imprints with forward Monte Carlo modelling.
AI.result: The two-wavelength approach successfully breaks degeneracies between physical processes, most notably distinguishing minor mergers, dry major mergers, and adiabatic expansion—mechanisms that produce ambiguous signatures in single-band optical SMR analyses. The combined rest-UV and optical view is demonstrated to be more constraining than individual band measurements.
AI.conclusion: The results motivate joint rest-UV and optical SMR measurements with current and upcoming wide-field imaging surveys, as the complementary stellar population tracers provide a powerful diagnostic of the physical processes that build galaxy structure.

title: The efficient star-forming regions of stripped-envelope supernovae
comment: Resubmitted to MNRAS after corrections. Main text: 10 pages, 2 figures, and 2 tables. Appendix: 3 pages, 2 figures, and 1 table
summary: Massive stars ($> 8~\rm{M}_{\odot}$) play a key role in shaping the interstellar medium of galaxies through stellar feedback. However, how these stars form and evolve before exploding as core-collapse supernovae (SNe) remains elusive. We compute for the first time the star-formation efficiencies (SFEs) at the locations of hydrogen-rich (H-rich) SNe and stripped-envelope SNe (SESNe) to constrain their progenitor properties. We used VLT/MUSE and ALMA observations of H$α$/H$β$ and CO(2-1) emission lines to trace the components of the warm ionised gas and cold molecular gas, respectively. Both observations resolve individual H II regions and giant molecular clouds at spatial resolutions on cloud-scales ($\sim$100 pc). This combined data allows us to compute the SFE from the star formation rate (SFR) and the molecular gas mass (M$_{\rm{mol}}$) as SFE = SFR/M$_{\rm{mol}}$. We find that SESNe explode in environments that are currently forming stars eight times more efficiently than those of H-rich SNe (higher SFR for SESNe with similar M$_{\rm{mol}}$). On one hand, this is consistent with the scenario in which the majority of SESNe are produced from very massive stars ($> 20~\rm{M}_{\odot}$) if the initial mass function is top-heavy. On the other hand, most of SESN progenitor channels are formed from interacting binaries ($< 20~\rm{M}_{\odot}$) if an increased binary system formation rate is connected with turbulences and, in turn, with the boost to SFE. Then, an increased binary fraction could explain the enhanced H$α$ luminosities. In summary, SESNe preferentially occur in regions of intense, efficient star formation rather than simply higher gas content.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the star-formation efficiencies (SFEs) at the locations of hydrogen-rich SNe and stripped-envelope SNe (SESNe) using VLT/MUSE Hα/Hβ and ALMA CO(2-1) observations at ~100 pc cloud-scale resolution. SESNe explode in environments forming stars 8 times more efficiently than H-rich SNe, suggesting either top-heavy IMF with very massive progenitors (>20 M⊙) or binary-formation scenarios with lower-mass progenitors (<20 M⊙) driven by turbulent, efficient star-forming regions.
AI.motivation: To constrain the progenitor properties of massive stars that explode as different types of core-collapse supernovae by measuring the local star-formation efficiencies at their explosion sites, which remain elusive despite the key role massive stars play in feedback.
AI.method: The study combines VLT/MUSE observations of Hα/Hβ emission lines (tracing warm ionised gas) and ALMA CO(2-1) observations (tracing cold molecular gas) to resolve individual H II regions and giant molecular clouds at ~100 pc scales. SFE is computed as SFE = SFR/M_mol from star formation rate and molecular gas mass measurements at each SN location.
AI.result: SESNe explode in environments with star formation efficiencies eight times higher than those of H-rich SNe, exhibiting higher SFRs for similar molecular gas masses. The enhanced Hα luminosities and SFE at SESNe locations support either a top-heavy IMF scenario with very massive single-star progenitors (>20 M⊙) or an interacting binary scenario with increased binary formation rates linked to turbulent, efficient star-forming conditions.
